subject: general
question: A can do a piece of work in 63 hours, B and C together can do it in 42 hours, while A and C together can do it in 27 hours. How long (in hours) will B alone take to do it?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total work = LCM(63, 42, 27) = 378 units.

Efficiencies: A = 6, B + C = 9, and A + C = 14.

Efficiency of C = (A + C) − A = 14 − 6 = 8.

Efficiency of B = (B + C) − C = 9 − 8 = 1.

Time taken by B = Total work ÷ B's efficiency = 378 ÷ 1 = 378 hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 378 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by A = 63 hours

Time taken by B and C together = 42 hours

Time taken by A and C together = 27 hours

**Formula Used:**

Total Work = LCM of given time

Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time

Time = Total Work ÷ Efficiency

**Calculations:**

⇒ Efficiency of A = 6 units/hour

⇒ Efficiency of A + C = 14 units/hour

⇒ Efficiency of C = 14 − 6 = 8 units/hour

⇒ Efficiency of B + C = 9 units/hour

⇒ Efficiency of B = 9 − 8 = 1 unit/hour

⇒ Time taken by B alone = Total Work ÷ Efficiency of B

⇒ Time taken by B alone = 378 ÷ 1 = 378 hours

**∴ The correct answer is 378 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Work & Efficiency Relationship

Efficiency is inversely proportional to the time taken. Total Work = Efficiency × Time. The LCM method simplifies fractional calculations by assigning whole numbers to the total assumed work.

Work & Wages

Wages are always distributed in proportion to the total work done by each individual. If workers work for the same number of days, the wages are distributed directly in the ratio of their efficiencies.

Pipes & Cisterns

This concept is exactly the same as Time & Work. Inlet pipes have a positive efficiency as they fill the tank, while outlet pipes or leaks have a negative efficiency as they empty the tank.
